correctness.rationale: Explicit 16-pair cover and three-output bound prove minimum cardinality six. A finite dynamic program by distinct subsets of 64 possible transmitted words gives exactly 644 full unions, validated by a separate pruned exhaustive six-loop count. Incidence counts split exactly 120 perfect covers and 524 with overlap, and a complete 48-action orbit computation yields 21 classes with sizes summing to 644. The checker source is supplied and replayed; no infinite statement is inferred.

originality.rationale: Xie–Sun–Ge (2026) treat deletion-covering bounds and constructions; Chee–Ge–Ling (2010) establish possible sizes and existence of perfect length-three codes. Neither supplies the claimed 644 labeled minimum covers, 524 non-perfect minima, 21 symmetry classes, or incidence-profile counts in inspected material. Cross-checked published-finding corpus and accessible own claim titles under parameter, alias and enumeration searches. Equivalent census in an unindexed directed-design source remains a real risk.
residual_risks: A quaternary exact directed covering-design enumeration in unindexed/older sources could already imply these 644 codebooks and the 21 orbits.
Global symbol relabeling and word reversal is one natural, specified group; under other equivalence groups the number of classes differs.

value.rationale: For the natural four-letter (DNA-sized) alphabet and smallest nontrivial deletion-covering space, the complete optimum-codebook census resolves a structural question not answered by the already known optimum size: most minimum covers overlap and are not deletion-correcting. The 21 orbit classes and complete overlap profiles distinguish genuinely different sharp-cover types and provide exact benchmarks for construction and classification, without claiming stronger asymptotic or error-correction properties.
